description: Attack the big dense shapes 6/7/11 with a contour-integral / rational-filter (FEAST-style) batched eigensolver — a mechanism distinct from the in-flight Chebyshev polynomial filter (brief-75) and sign-DC (brief-76). For each spectral window, approximate the spectral projector by a quadrature sum of resolvents sum_j w_j (A - z_j I)^-1 applied to a random block B (a few complex/real shifted linear solves via batched Cholesky/LU on (A - z_j I), all batched and GEMM/solve-heavy on tensor cores), giving the window subspace; orthonormalize (3xTF32 CQR), Rayleigh-Ritz the small projected block, assemble across windows. Resolvent-based spectrum slicing has no per-column tridiag sync. Per-matrix residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback. Route the n=512/1024 dense-class shapes.

FEAST resolvent full-decomp mechanism built + wired behind shape-11 guard (n=512 homog high-PR non-2-level). W=4 windows x q=8 GL nodes on circular contours, real-SPD form (M^2+y^2 I Cholesky+solve per conjugate node), 2 FEAST subspace iters, global residual-topk assembly. VALIDATES 39/39. Profile: solve/GEMM-bound (batch_trsm+potrf+tf32gemm dominate, ZERO tridiag/sytrd sync) -- mechanism is as designed. BUT gapless even spectrum -> orth=7.57 (gate 4.6e-3), eigr_rel=0.45 (gate 9.2e-3), 640/640 fall back to cuSOLVER. Shape11 1095237us (sign-DC 99725us); geomean 34348us (parent 28561). Measured crossover: independent-window+global-topk assembly double-counts boundary eigenvectors on a gapless spectrum -> non-orthogonal Q. Next: disjoint per-window membership select.

Fixed the resolvent filter SIGN BUG (A-zI=M-iyI so Re[w(A-zI)^-1]=[Re(w)M-Im(w)y]S, not +Im(w)y). W=2 overlapping-contour split (resolvent analogue of sign-DC median split): each contour widened by ovl=0.5 so gapless-spectrum boundary eigenvalues are INTERIOR (W>=4 razor-edge boundaries measured unfixable). Disjoint per-window membership by Ritz value + CQR2 dedupe of near-median duplicates. Now FULLY DECOMPOSES the gapless even spectrum: 39/39 validate, eigr~1e-3, nbad=1/640. Profile: batch_trsm(Cholesky-solve)+potrf dominate (~21%), solve/GEMM-bound as designed, zero tridiag. MEASURED CROSSOVER: shape11 1323143us vs sign-DC 99725us (~13x slower) -- the 48 full-n Cholesky+solves at m~408 rhs + two 408-wide cuSOLVER Ritz eighs are the wall. geomean 34858us. Next: route Ritz eigh to megakernel (m<=448), cut solve count.

Factorization caching: per-node Cholesky of M^2+y^2 I done ONCE/window (was once/apply) -> reused across the 3 FEAST subspace-iter applies. Also probed Ritz-via-megakernel (leaked 150/640 on wide 408-block TF32 backtransform, reverted to cuSOLVER). shape11 ~1212446us (vs t2 1323143), geomean 34697us. CONFIRMED CROSSOVER across ~20 configs: the wide-m cholesky_SOLVE (trsm, m~400, per-apply, un-cacheable) dominates; W=2 forces m>=256 (half-spectrum)+overlap; cheapest passing config still ~950us-1.2s ~10x sign-DC's 100ms. The resolvent mechanism cannot beat Newton-Schulz sign-DC on the gapless FULL decomposition -- sign-DC's split is 36 GEMMs (~10ms) vs FEAST's 16-24 full-n Cholesky+solves (~300ms floor). Next: test narrow-window regime on concentrated/mixed spectra (shapes 6/7).

BUILT + wired + measured the FEAST contour-integral/rational-filter batched eigensolver (3 trials, HEAD 81fef69c5, geomean 34697us vs parent 28561us). MECHANISM WORKS: real-SPD resolvent form (M^2+y^2 I Cholesky+solve per collapsed conjugate node), W=2 overlapping-contour split (resolvent analogue of sign-DC median split), disjoint per-window membership + CQR2 dedupe, factorization cached across FEAST subspace iters. Validates 39/39, eigr~1e-3, nbad=1-2/640 on the gapless even spectrum. Profiled solve/GEMM-bound EXACTLY as the brief posited (batch_trsm + potrf + tf32gemm dominate, ZERO tridiag/sytrd sync). Fixed a filter SIGN BUG en route (A-zI=M-iyI). PER-SHAPE: shape11(lapdense_even512,routed to FEAST W=2/q=4/subit=3)=1232423us vs sign-DC 99725us (12.4x SLOWER); shapes 6(mixed512)=107713us and 7(mixed1024)=106833us UNCHANGED (they route to mixed-peel; FEAST's homogeneity guard correctly excludes heterogeneous batches). MEASURED CROSSOVER (confirmed across ~25 configs): the mechanism CANNOT beat cuSOLVER/sign-DC on a FULL gapless decomposition -- extracting an n/2-dim subspace needs solves with >=n/2 RHS, each requiring a full-n Cholesky factorization (~4ms) + wide-m trsm (~10ms); W=2 forces m~256+overlap~400, and 16-24 node-solves are needed for accuracy -> ~950ms-1.2s floor, ~10-13x sign-DC's ~10ms-of-GEMMs split. Narrow-window (m=64) single apply is 30ms (6x under cuSOLVER's 191ms) BUT only helps a low-rank subspace, which the existing low-rank peel already does faster via A@A GEMM (no Cholesky). Complex-arithmetic form probed 2.4x slower/node than real-SPD (condition-squaring is cheaper than complex LU). OPEN DIRECTIONS (unbuilt): (1) Zolotarev-optimal rational weights for a sharper filter at fewer poles -- but boundary contamination on gapless spectra is intrinsic, unlikely to change the count budget; (2) resolvent as a narrow-window DEFLATION assist stacked on sign-DC (peel a hard near-zero cluster, sign-DC the rest) -- niche, off the current full-solver framing; (3) FEAST only on the CONCENTRATED subset of mixed shapes 6/7 -- but that duplicates the mixed-peel and inherits the Cholesky wall. RECOMMENDATION for the manager: FEAST regresses shape 11 and does not apply to 6/7 under a safe guard; do not pick trial-3 as a parent for the geomean. The resolvent lever is dominated by the factorization-per-node wall for full decompositions at these n. If pursued, only the narrow-window deflation-assist (direction 2) has an unmeasured chance; the wide-window full-solver is a measured dead-weight vs sign-DC. The parent 980c88b (sign-DC + mixed-peel + low-rank) remains the frontier for these shapes.

DEFLATION-ASSIST (open #2) built + measured. Profiler-first target: sign-DC on shape11 is 42% dominated by the mega_eigh_med_split_k leaf (38.5ms, the 2x300 reduced-block eigh). Built _feast_deflate_signdc: peel the two OUTER |lambda| bands via narrow resolvent windows (2 windows x q=4), project out via (I-QpQp^T)A(I-QpQp^T), sign-DC the deflated remainder, merge+Ritz+sort, full gate+fallback. CORRECT: eigr 1.4e-5, orth 4.2e-5, 0/640 fallback. But 8.26x sign-DC end-to-end (803479us vs 97299us): peel-only=68ms of the 97ms budget (8 full-n=512 Choleskys ~32ms + wide-ish solves), and the deflated remainder is still ~448-dim so sign-DC's leaf barely shrinks. Route DISABLED (_FEAST_DEFLATE_ENABLED=False) + full-solve FEAST disabled (_FEAST_ENABLED=False) -> geomean 28562us == parent 28561, NO regression on any shape. SPECTRUM CHECK ruled out Candidate B: shape11 even spectrum is UNIFORM (min gap 0.00196 == median, no peelable cluster); shape7 has only ISOLATED degeneracies (min gap 1.7e-11, median 4e-4), not a cluster. Zolotarev vs GL: GL already sharp (transition 0.39 vs trap 1.03 at q=4); a sharper filter cannot reduce the per-node Cholesky count, so it does not change the economics. MAP (where the narrow resolvent does/does NOT pay): narrow window m=64/q=4 = 30782us at n=512 b640, dominated by q=4 full-n Choleskys (~4.75ms each); the low-rank peel's core A@A GEMM = 285us -> the resolvent window is 108x the GEMM, so the existing A@A-GEMM dominant-subspace peel dominates the resolvent EVERYWHERE a concentrated subspace is extractable. The resolvent primitive only avoids a full eigh when the subspace is narrow, but any narrow-subspace extraction is done cheaper by the GEMM peel (no Cholesky). CONCLUSION: no target among 6/7/11 where the narrow-window resolvent beats the incumbent; the Cholesky-per-node cost dominates both the full solve and the deflation assist.

Pursued the deflation-assist lever (open #2) profiler-first, per coordinator direction. HEAD 3065e6383, geomean 28562us == parent 28561 (NO regression: both FEAST routes disabled; the full-solve config that regressed shape11 12x is OFF the live route, machinery dormant). 4 trials: t1-t3 mapped the full-solve crossover; t4 built + measured the narrow-window deflation assist. FINDINGS: (A) profiled sign-DC on shape11 -> 42% is the mega_eigh_med_split_k leaf (38.5ms, 2x300 reduced-block eigh) = the bottleneck. Built _feast_deflate_signdc (peel 2 outer |lambda| bands via narrow resolvent windows -> deflate (I-P)A(I-P) -> sign-DC remainder -> merge/Ritz/sort, full gate+fallback). CORRECT (eigr 1.4e-5, 0/640 fallback) but 8.26x sign-DC (803479 vs 97299us): peel-ONLY is 68ms of the 97ms budget (8 full-n Choleskys) and the deflated remainder stays ~448-dim so the leaf barely shrinks. (B) Candidate B ruled out by spectrum analysis: shape11 spectrum is UNIFORM (min gap==median 0.00196, no cluster); shape7 has isolated degeneracies (min gap 1.7e-11) not a peelable cluster. (C) Zolotarev/GL: GL already sharp (transition 0.39 @ q=4); sharper filter can't cut the per-node Cholesky count. THE MAP (where the resolvent primitive does/doesnt pay): narrow window m=64/q=4 = 30782us at n=512 b640, dominated by q full-n Choleskys (~4.75ms each). The low-rank peel's core A@A GEMM = 285us -> the resolvent window is 108x the GEMM. So the existing A@A-GEMM dominant-subspace peel DOMINATES the resolvent everywhere a concentrated subspace is extractable, and cuSOLVER/sign-DC dominate the full/gapless decomposition. The resolvent's structural cost (a full-n Cholesky FACTORIZATION per quadrature node, ~4-5ms, paid regardless of window width m) is the wall: it makes the primitive lose to a GEMM-based peel for narrow subspaces AND to sign-DC's GEMM-split for wide ones. There is NO regime among shapes 6/7/11 where a resolvent (full-solve or deflation-assist) beats the incumbent. RECOMMENDATION: the resolvent mechanism is comprehensively mapped as dominated on these shapes; the parent 980c88b (sign-DC + mixed-peel + low-rank) remains the frontier. The only theoretically-open resolvent niche would be a matrix class with a WIDE spectral GAP isolating a MODERATE cluster (so few nodes + narrow-ish m + a genuinely gap-separated remainder) -- none of 6/7/11 has this. Suggest the manager point remaining workers at non-resolvent levers (the sign-DC leaf megakernel barrier-bound 38.5ms cost is the real shape-11 bottleneck -> a faster reduced-block base solver, e.g. a batched tensor-core tridiag or a cluster-megakernel widening, would directly attack it).
